title: Which app profile a device gets: rule order, groups and the longest match

prose.text: Each platform has its own list of profile rules, and a device receives one of them. {{enrollment-download}} {{ascending-precedence}} {{first-applicable}}

prose.label: Who a rule names.
prose.text: {{user-groups}} {{group-all-docstring}} The API document says all device groups instead: [[zcc.api.web-policy-wire:group-all-scope]]. {{users-limit}} {{device-group-versions}} {{unassigned-rule}} Whether `groupAll` makes a populated group list irrelevant, and whether a disabled device-group switch ignores its list, is open {{gap:group-flags}}.

prose.label: The default policy.
prose.text: {{default-policy-page}} When a device receives it, and how it appears in the API, is open {{gap:default-policy}}.
Whether the rule order numbers must be contiguous is open {{gap:rule-order-contiguity}}.
A device keeps the profile it downloaded until it downloads again: [[zcc.app-profiles.propagation]].

checks.do: List the enabled rules for the device's platform that name the user, one of the user's groups, or all groups.
If one of those rules also names the device's device group, it wins over a lower-numbered rule that matches the user group only.
Otherwise the applicable rule with the lowest rule order applies.
If no rule applies, the platform's default policy; how that is chosen is open.

enrollment-download.statement: When a user enrolls, the app uses the order of precedence and the user's identity to download an app profile with the appropriate policy rule.

quotes: When a user enrolls the app with the Zscaler service, the app uses the order of precedence and identity of the user to download an app profile with the appropriate policy rule.

ascending-precedence.statement: The rule order is the order of precedence among a platform's profile rules and determines which rule the app downloads for a user; precedence is by ascending number.

evidence.after: The Add Windows Policy window appears.
quotes: The rule order reflects the order of precedence among configured profile policy rules and helps determine which rule the app downloads for a user upon enrollment. Precedence is based on ascending numerical order.

first-applicable.statement: The vendor's example walks the rules in order: the app checks whether rule 1 applies to the user, moves on to rule 2 and, finding that it applies, downloads that rule's profile.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector begins by checking whether rule 1 applies to the user.
The app moves on to rule 2 and upon determining it applies to the user, downloads the profile containing the appropriate policy rule.

disabled-not-enforced.statement: A rule whose status is Disabled is not enforced.

evidence.after: The Add Windows Policy window appears.
quotes: Select Disabled to inactivate the rule or select Enabled to activate the rule. If you don't enable the rule, the policy rule is not enforced.

longest-match.statement: If a user's group is assigned to two profiles and one of them also names a device group, the app applies the profile matching both the user group and the device group, because the longest match has priority, regardless of rule order.

evidence.after: The Add Windows Policy window appears.
quotes: If a user belongs to the same user group that is assigned to two different profiles and one of the profiles is assigned a device group, then Zscaler Client Connector applies the app profile matching both the user group and device group (because the longest match has priority) regardless of the rule order.

user-groups.statement: A rule names selected user groups (with no limit on how many) or all groups; newly added groups are selected automatically and must be cleared to exclude them. Groups are synced from Internet & SaaS and may not appear if it is not enabled and configured.

evidence.after: The Add Windows Policy window appears.
quotes: When new user groups are added, they are automatically selected. You can clear the checkbox to exclude them from your policy.
There is no limit to the number of groups you can select.
Click All to select all groups.
Groups are synced from Internet & SaaS, and are only available when Internet & SaaS is enabled and configured.

group-all-docstring.statement: The Python SDK documents `group_all` as 0 or 1: whether the policy applies to all groups.

quotes: whether the policy applies to all groups.

users-limit.statement: A rule can also name specific users, up to 50; none are selected by default.

evidence.after: The Add Windows Policy window appears.
quotes: You can select up to 50 users. By default, no users are selected.

device-group-versions.statement: A rule can name device groups; on mobile they require Client Connector 4.5 or later for iOS and 3.7 or later for Android.

evidence.after: The Add Windows Policy window appears.
quotes: Device Groups: Select this option to apply this rule to specific groups or to all device groups.
Device groups are available only on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5 and later for iOS devices.
Device groups are available only on Zscaler Client Connector version 3.7 and later for Android devices.

unassigned-rule.statement: A rule can be saved with no user or user group, to create it before applying it.

evidence.after: The Add Windows Policy window appears.
quotes: Don't select a user or a user group if you want to create and save a rule before applying it to a user or a user group.

default-policy-page.statement: Each platform's App Profiles page shows a default policy alongside the configured rules.

quotes: View a list of all configured app profile rules.

name-lists.statement: Besides the ID lists, the API document's web policy edit body has string-array name lists: `userNames`, `groupNames`, `deviceGroupNames`, `appIdentityNames` and `appServiceNames`. It does not describe them.
name-lists.conditions: Added (verifier w2 A15): these keys had been dropped as generated, but the generated layer does not carry them; the API document gives types only.

default-policy.title: When the default app profile applies, and where it lives in the API
default-policy.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "A null sub-policy means 'no platform-specific policy defined' — not 'inherit defaults.' Devices on an unscoped platform fall through to the tenant's default Web Policy", and "If the tenant default policy is permissive, this can be a security gap." The help shows a default policy per platform but not when a device receives it (no rule matches the user, or no rule exists), nor whether the API shows it as a flagged record, the last rule, or a separate setting. A Go SDK test comment (a test comment, not documentation) says a list response can carry ID 0, for example the default policy, and that a GET by ID 0 is not supported.
default-policy.blocks: answers about which settings an unmatched user or device gets

quotes: ID 0 is valid in list responses (e.g. default policy); GET-by-id for 0 is not supported by the API.

group-flags.title: Whether groupAll and a disabled device-group switch override populated lists
group-flags.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "group_all = true with non-empty group_ids — the broader flag takes priority at enforcement time; group_ids is effectively ignored. Same for enable_device_groups = false with a populated device_group_ids list." The sources also disagree on what `groupAll` covers: the API document says all device groups, the Python SDK all groups (divergence group-all-scope in zcc.api.web-policy-wire).
group-flags.blocks: audits that flag a rule's group list as dormant

rule-order-contiguity.title: Whether app profile rule order must be contiguous
rule-order-contiguity.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "The portal does not enforce contiguous ordering", with the advice to number rules with gaps (10, 20, 30). The help has the rule order chosen from a drop-down, which suggests the console offers only existing positions; neither is stated.
rule-order-contiguity.blocks: scripts that insert a rule at a chosen position
